chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said:
Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the Black Stone: 'Do people fight over it if they become numerous?' He said, 'If that is the case, then gesture with your hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on touching the Black Stone if crowds are dense and fighting occurs?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) provides a pragmatic concession for the Black Stone, ruling that when crowds become dense and lead to conflict, a simple hand gesture suffices to fulfill the ritual obligation. This highlights the Shia principle of *raḥma* (mercy) and avoiding harm (*darar*) in religious practice, prioritizing the spirit of reverence over rigid physical contact when necessary. The ruling underscores the flexibility within *fiqh* to accommodate changing social conditions during the Hajj.
